snippet.title: Men, Insecurity, and the Bible Passage Everyone Avoids
snippet.description:
Bryan and Jordan are joined by special guests Elijah Stanley and Alyssa McCutchan for a unique conversation on insecurity, discipleship, biblical manhood, and one of the most debated passages in the New Testament. Elijah shares his personal story featured in Bryan’s new book and opens up about isolation, shame, mentorship, and finding identity as a son of God. 

Alyssa offers a powerful perspective on why discipling young men deeply impacts women, families, and the health of the church. They also walk through 1 Timothy 2:8–15 and discuss how Christians should approach difficult Bible passages with humility, context, and trust in Scripture. 

Bryan’s new book, Built for More, releases Monday, May 18.

snippet.title: Why Men Need Mentors, Doctrine, and Brotherhood
snippet.description: This episode explores how men are actually formed through discipleship, sound doctrine, and spiritual relationships. Bryan and Jordan discuss the relationship between Paul and Timothy, why so many men feel spiritually stuck, the myths and distractions that keep men passive, and why biblical truth is essential for courage, leadership, and conviction. They also unpack the role of spiritual fatherhood, mentorship, and the importance of men being both led and leading others.

snippet.title: Biblical Manhood Starts With This: Why Men Need Role Models
snippet.description: What does it actually mean to be a man and why do so many men feel unsure of their identity? In this episode, we unpack the role model crisis shaping a generation, and why biblical manhood isn’t formed in isolation. From the voices that shaped us to the ones we’re missing, we talk about how identity is formed, why so many men feel stuck, and how the right people in your life can call out who God created you to be. If you’ve ever felt directionless or unsure of your role as a man, this conversation gets to the root and points toward a better way forward.

snippet.title: Why You Need Spiritual Family More Than You Think
snippet.description:
In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, we explore why following Jesus was never meant to be done alone. From our connection with the Confluence family of churches to the heart behind shared mission and church planting, we talk about the power of spiritual family and doing ministry together.

We also dive into the importance of brotherhood in a culture that pushes isolation and why real growth requires vulnerability, accountability, and intentional relationships. Finally, we unpack prayer as the language of dependence and what it looks like to truly connect with God in a deeper, more personal way.

snippet.title: Your Story Matters: How to Share Your Faith Without Fear
snippet.description:
In this episode, we reflect on a powerful celebration of life and the impact of a faith that endures beyond death, along with a few cultural moments shaping the conversation right now.

The heart of this episode centers on a simple challenge. Most believers have a story, but many struggle to share it. We unpack how boldness flows from nearness to Jesus, not pressure or performance. Through practical tools like BLESS and real life examples, we talk about what it looks like to share your faith in everyday spaces.

Finally, we address a deeper cultural lie about happiness and purpose. What if fulfillment is not found in creating your own path, but in living for something greater and helping others thrive?

This episode is a call to live boldly and trust that your story matters.

snippet.title: Faith, Truth, and Cultural Confusion: Getting the Bible Right Again
snippet.description:
In this episode, we briefly reflect on Easter and the reality that doubt has always surrounded the resurrection, just as it did for people like Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea.

The core of the conversation centers on how truth is being handled today. We unpack the difference between misusing Scripture and distorting it, and why that distinction matters. Looking at real cultural examples, we talk about how the Bible is often used to support ideas it was never meant to, and what it looks like to interpret it faithfully.

We also explore the tension of boldness and wisdom in young believers and the importance of real discipleship. Passion without formation can lead to unnecessary harm, even when the intent is right.

Finally, we address a deeper issue many men are facing today. Without affirmation and direction, men often withdraw or react in unhealthy ways. What does it look like to call men up and form them with truth and purpose?

This episode is a call to hold firmly to truth while intentionally developing people to live it out well.

#BibleTruth #ChristianPodcast #FaithAndCulture #Discipleship #ChurchLeadership #Masculinity #ChristianMen #TruthMatters #BiblicalTeaching #FollowJesus #LeadershipDevelopment

snippet.title: 10 Objections to the Resurrection… and Why They Don’t Hold Up
snippet.description:
As Holy Week begins, Bryan and Jordan reflect on what this season means and why it still matters by looking ahead to Good Friday and Easter while inviting us to keep Jesus at the center. They also share updates on upcoming worship moments and the Good Men Conference, including a new resource for young men.

The conversation then turns to truth in a culture full of distortion. They unpack how ideas like individualism, prosperity, and cultural narratives can reshape the gospel, and respond to popular claims about Jesus, sexuality, abortion, and even the nature of God. With Scripture often quoted but redefined, they highlight why clarity around truth is more important than ever.

To anchor it all, they walk through common objections to the resurrection and make a compelling case for its historical credibility. Because if Jesus truly rose from the dead, it changes everything... not just during Holy Week, but for all of life.

snippet.title: Why Truth Is Disappearing… and Why It Matters More Than Ever
snippet.description:
What does it actually look like to finish your life well? In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Bryan and Jordan reflect on the life and impact of Confluence pastor Rhys Scott and how his example connects deeply to Paul’s words in Acts 20. Their conversation moves beyond theory into the kind of life that is marked by faithfulness, endurance, and a clear sense of calling.

As they wrestle with what it takes to stay the course, the discussion turns personal; exploring the habits, convictions, and decisions that shape a life that finishes strong. Along the way, they unpack how truth plays a central role in truly knowing God and others, and why clarity around truth matters more than ever in a culture where it is often distorted.

Jordan shares some of his own experiences growing in confidence when it comes to speaking truth, especially with those who don’t yet believe. The episode closes by addressing a pressing question: what should concern us most about the way truth is being reshaped in our world today, and how do we respond as followers of Jesus?

This is a thoughtful and challenging conversation for anyone who wants their life to count, not just for now, but for the long run.

snippet.title: Creating a Healthy Family Culture
snippet.description:
In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Bryan Mowrey is joined by special guests Willy and Sofi Verduzco from Origen Church in Guadalajara, Mexico, one of the catalytic churches in the Confluence family. They begin with an honest update on the current situation in Guadalajara and the realities of ministering in a region affected by cartel activity, sharing how the gospel continues to move forward even in challenging circumstances.

The conversation then turns to technology. As leaders who have built a large online following while reaching people far beyond their city, Willy and Sofi talk about how they’ve learned to use digital tools intentionally without allowing them to dominate their lives, especially as we enter a season of digital fasting as a church.

Bryan also explores how they cultivate a healthy culture in their home. Willy and Sofi share practical insight into building a strong marriage, raising children with purpose, and shaping a family culture centered on Jesus while leading a growing church.

They close by reflecting on what excites them most about the future of the Confluence family of churches and where they see God leading us in the years ahead, especially the growing opportunity to reach and develop Spanish-speaking leaders and churches throughout the world.

It’s a conversation full of wisdom, faith, and vision for what God is doing across nations.

snippet.title: Knowledge Is Everywhere. Wisdom Is Rare.
snippet.description:
After discussing the exciting week ahead at Confluence Leadership Conference and reflecting on ministry partnerships in Mexico, the conversation turns toward something deeper: the kind of wisdom our generation desperately needs. We live in a moment where access to information is endless, yet biblical wisdom often feels scarce.

What does it actually mean when Proverbs tells us to “get wisdom”? How do we pursue it? We talk through the difference between knowledge and wisdom, the role surrender plays in shaping mature disciples, and why submission isn’t weakness but participation in the life of God and His church. From Scripture to social media, we explore how our sources of influence form us and how reordering them may be one of the most important spiritual decisions we make.

snippet.title: Wisdom v. Information
What Does the Bible Say About Gambling?
snippet.description:
In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Bryan Mowrey and Jordan Dillon explore how the biblical theme of light vs darkness applies to our modern digital lives. As Jubilee Church begins a digital fast and continues the “Faithful Disciples in a Digital World” series, they reflect on how our phones, devices, and constant connectivity are shaping our attention, desires, and spiritual formation in ways previous generations never experienced.

Rather than simply asking how to avoid sin, Bryan and Jordan challenge listeners to consider how a deeper love for Christ reshapes our habits, focus, and daily lives. They discuss the difference between being exposed to darkness and participating in it, why Christians are called to be bright rather than just loud, and how fixing our eyes on what is good protects our hearts from cynicism, distraction, and spiritual drift. They also address specific cultural realities like gambling and digital temptation, and share what they’re seeing in the life of our church as people intentionally step away from digital noise to pursue greater clarity and devotion.

This conversation is both honest and hopeful, inviting you to examine your relationship with technology and encouraging you to live as a faithful disciple who reflects the light of Christ in a world increasingly shaped by screens.

snippet.title: Connection v. Distraction
Light v. Darkness
The Church & Immigration in a Divided America | Biblical Perspective
snippet.description:
In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Bryan Mowrey and Jordan Dillon discuss how Christians should think about immigration, government authority, civil disobedience, and cultural pressure.

We explore biblical wisdom for engaging controversial topics, navigating social media, responding to injustice, and staying rooted in Christ in a polarized age.

Topics include:
• Immigration and Christian compassion
• Government authority and biblical obedience
• Civil disobedience and protest
• Social media and public opinion
• Prophetic vs pastoral responsibility
• Finding peace in a rage-driven culture

If you’ve been wrestling with how to follow Jesus in today’s political and cultural climate, this conversation is for you.

snippet.title: Fullness v. Emptiness
More Assurance: Perseverance in Failure
Foster Care, Faith & Family: A Conversation with Ryan MacDonald
snippet.description:
In this episode, host Jordan Dillon sits down with Ryan MacDonald from Foster the City for an honest, practical conversation about adoption, foster care, and learning to love vulnerable children as a family and a church.

Ryan shares his personal journey into adopting and fostering, how his family is shaped today, and why partnering with organizations like Foster the City matters. Jordan and Ryan talk through the biggest hurdles people face when considering foster care, how to discern if this is the right time for your family, and what healthy preparation looks like for parents stepping into this season.

They also discuss the encouraging trends Ryan is seeing in the foster community, the concerns leaders should be paying attention to, and how everyday believers can stay connected and supportive even if they’re not fostering themselves.

Whether you're exploring foster care, supporting someone who is, or wanting to better understand the needs of vulnerable children, this episode offers grounded wisdom, lived experience, and hope for the future.

snippet.title: Breastplate of Righteousness
Standing Firm: Understanding Spiritual Warfare in Today’s World
snippet.description: In this week’s episode, Bryan and Jordan sit down for a candid conversation on spiritual warfare and what it means to “put on the armor of God.” They explore why the West often underestimates spiritual opposition, how accusations and division are tactics of the enemy, and what it means to “stand firm” in the armor of God. A timely conversation for anyone who senses the battle heating up around them.

snippet.title: Godly Singles and the Church as Family
snippet.description: What does it look like to live faithfully and purposefully as a single Christian? In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, host Jordan Dillon sits down with Greg Nelson, elder at our St. Louis City location, for a thoughtful conversation on singleness, wisdom, and the family of God. Together they reflect on the advice they would give their younger single selves, how singles can better leverage their season, and the vital role the church plays as a spiritual family. Greg also shares how he and his wife have intentionally included singles in their home life, what that looked like practically, and why it matters for both singles and married couples alike. Whether you’re single, married, or walking alongside others in the church, this episode offers encouragement and biblical wisdom to help you see singleness not as a waiting room but as a valuable season for growth, purpose, and kingdom impact.

snippet.title: Godly Singles
Godly Wives and Biblical Marriage feat. Lissy Dillon and Rachel Mowrey
snippet.description:
What does it mean to be a godly wife, and how does that shape a marriage that honors Christ? In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, host Jordan Dillon and his wife Lissy sit down with Lead Pastor Bryan Mowrey and his wife Rachel for an honest, biblical, and practical conversation about marriage. They share stories of what first drew them to one another and the role of community in choosing a spouse, reflect on the power of a wife’s words to either build up or tear down her husband, and wrestle with questions of ambition, direction, and decision-making in marriage. 
The conversation digs into what biblical submission really looks like (and what it isn’t) while also exploring how couples can balance home life, work, and kingdom priorities. Along the way, they discuss how to process shortcomings, navigate seasons of failure, and ultimately keep Christ at the center of their relationship. Whether you’re single, newly married, or years into marriage, this episode will encourage you to trust God’s design for marriage and to find hope in His goodness.

👉 Watch Bryan’s referenced sermon “Calling All Leaders” from the story of Deborah here: https://vimeo.com/353247792

snippet.title: Godly Wives
Political Violence and Division: How Should Christians Respond?
snippet.description: In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, host Jordan Dillon and lead pastor Bryan Mowrey reflect on a heavy week marked by tragedy—the violent murder of a woman on a train, the assassination of Charlie Kirk, and the recent school shooting. They explore how Christians can respond in the midst of violence, grief, and political tension, asking what it looks like to honor others in a hostile culture, to walk in boldness without losing love, and to discern the reality of spiritual warfare in our day. Along the way, they wrestle with questions about social media’s influence, whether the church is becoming “too political,” and how Jesus calls us to love our enemies.

snippet.title: Husbands: Leadership, Responsibility, and Marriage Today
snippet.description: This episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast zeroes in on the unique calling of men as husbands and leaders in the home. Bryan and Jordan tackle the false dichotomy of men versus women, unpack the heart of biblical servant leadership, and discuss how husbands can resist the tendency to avoid responsibility. The conversation addresses the challenges of toxic masculinity, how to lead well in today’s culture, the realities of divorce, and even the shifting age of marriage. If you’re a husband—or desire to be one—this episode offers clarity, encouragement, and a biblical vision for leading with love and faithfulness.

snippet.title: Urgency, Confusion, & the Power of Spiritual Gifts
snippet.description: In this episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Lead Pastor Bryan Mowrey joins host Jordan Dillon to unpack the vital role of spiritual gifts in the life of every believer. Together, they explore why spiritual gifts are often misunderstood, how to discern the right and wrong ways of using them, and the urgency of stewarding the gifts God has given us. The conversation also dives into the biblical standard for practicing spiritual gifts, the boldness we need to step out in faith, and which gifts are often overlooked in today’s church. Bryan also offers practical insight on pursuing the gift of prophecy and why it matters for building up the body of Christ.

snippet.title: Biblical Wisdom for Money, Budgeting & God’s Provision
snippet.description: In this special bonus episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Lead Pastor Bryan Mowrey joins host Jordan Dillon for a conversation on money, stewardship, and faith. Together they unpack what the Bible teaches about our relationship with money and how it shapes our lives in ways we often don’t realize. Bryan shares practical frameworks for budgeting and financial stewardship, helping us move from ignorance to wisdom in how we handle money. The discussion also dives into what it truly means to trust God as provider—bringing clarity, encouragement, and hope to a topic that touches every area of life.

snippet.description:
Every generation faces defining moments—so what is God calling His church to do right now? Bryan Mowrey unpacks how we can recognize and leverage the opportunities God has placed before us, rather than just going through the motions of everyday life.

The conversation closes with a powerful discussion on how to orient your life around the will of God.

Whether you’re a parent, mentor, or simply seeking wisdom for daily life, this episode is packed with practical insight and biblical perspective.

Whether you’re looking for encouragement, spiritual insight, or practical next steps in your faith, this episode will challenge and inspire you.

snippet.title: Letting Go, Standing Firm, and Making Wise Decisions: Bonus Podcast Episode with Bryan Mowrey
snippet.description: In this special bonus episode of the Jubilee Church Podcast, Lead Pastor Bryan Mowrey is joined by host Jordan Dillon for a wide-ranging conversation on topics that matter deeply to Christians today. They tackle how to let go of the past, how to make wise decisions in relationships and major life choices, what the Bible teaches about rewards, and how to stand firm in a culture that often challenges biblical values—especially around abortion and LGBTQ+ issues. They also address concerns about nominal Christianity and what it means to truly follow Jesus. We hope you enjoy!
